title: Placement release after a tray-chip arm click is judged against a stale press — arming can drop an unintended router
detail: app.press is only captured when a LEFT press lands while already placing; the chip-arm click returns before setting it. The arming click's release still enters the placement branch and compares against a stale press — if the previous placement click was within 6 px of the tray, an unintended router drops under the tray. start_run also never resets press.
recommended_fix: Set app.press to the current cursor when arming/cancelling placement (and reset in start_run), or require the originating press to have been a placement press before allowing a drop.

title: Span error label still says 'standard tier' after the tray made the draw tier selectable
evidence:
case .Span_Exceeds_Tier: return "too far for the standard tier"
...
+				if i < len(app.cat.pipe_tiers) {
+					app.tier = u16(i)
+					app.placing = -1
detail: The drag tier is now user-selectable via tray link chips (app.tier = u16(i)), but the Span_Exceeds_Tier rejection label still hardcodes 'standard tier' — a too-long draw on a non-standard tier gets mislabeled copy.
recommended_fix: Return the selected tier's id (app.cat.pipe_tiers[app.tier].id) in the label, or drop the tier name entirely ('too far for that tier').

title: Unknown_Node_Type added to Edit_Error but gets no reject_label case
evidence:
+	Unknown_Node_Type,  // 3.5 — placement type_idx out of catalog range
...
 	case .Span_Exceeds_Tier: return "too far for the standard tier"
 	case .Missing_Node: return "no node there"
 	case .Unknown_Tier: return "unknown tier"
+	case .Router_Ports_Full: return "router ports full — demolish a pipe or upgrade"
+	case .Invalid_Placement: return "can't place there — too close to a node or off-map"
+	case .Not_A_Junction: return "only routers are placeable from the tray"
 	}
detail: validate_place returns .Unknown_Node_Type for an out-of-range type_idx (pinned by test_place_rejects_unknown_type), but reject_label adds a case for every other new error and none for this one — it silently falls through to the generic 'can't do that'.
recommended_fix: Add a case for .Unknown_Node_Type (e.g. 'unknown node type'), or document that it is unreachable from the app so the omission is deliberate.
